term.def: Grounding means making an AI tool answer from your own trusted documents and data, instead of only from what it learned in training. It helps cut down wrong answers.

prompt.prompt: Act as a careful analyst. Use only the [document or data] I paste below to answer [your question]. If the answer is not in it, say so clearly and do not guess.

quiz.q: Express Computer reports that India's AI race is becoming an infrastructure race.
quiz.why: This restates the headline. It shows that AI depends on more than software.

quiz.q: If an AI tool sounds confident, its answer must be correct.
quiz.why: AI tools can sound sure even when they are wrong. Always check important facts.

quiz.q: AI is only useful for big companies with large tech teams.
quiz.why: Everyday chat tools are used by small teams too. You do not need a big tech department to start.

quiz.q: Visual Studio Magazine reports that Microsoft has added a Work IQ retrieval tool to ground AI agents in enterprise data.
quiz.why: This restates the headline. Grounding links AI answers to a company's own data.

quiz.q: Giving an AI tool clear context and an example of what you want usually improves its answer.
quiz.why: AI tools respond to the detail you give them. Vague requests tend to get vague answers.
